items.title: FG seeks Israeli expertise to strengthen border security, combat cross-border crimes
items.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has sought Israeli expertise in border security as part of efforts to curb cross-border crimes and strengthen national security. The move was disclosed in a press statement issued on Monday by the Special Assistant on Communication and New Media to the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Magnus Eze, following a valedictory visit by the outgoing Israeli Ambassador to Nigeria, Michael Freeman, to the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, at the ministry’s headquarters in Abuja. According to the statement, Odumegwu-Ojukwu reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to deepening collaboration with Israel in critical areas of security, including counter-terrorism, intelligence gathering, information sharing, security financing and capacity building for security personnel. The minister said Nigeria was looking to leverage Israeli expertise in border security to address the growing challenge of cross-border crimes and enhance the country’s overall security architecture. She noted that the administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had continued to prioritise security as a key driver of national development, stressing that sustainable progress could not be achieved without a secure environment. She said, “The President emphasises security everywhere he goes because you are actually going nowhere without security”. The minister also described the recent rescue of the Oriire schoolchildren by Nigerian security forces as a watershed moment in the country’s fight against insecurity. Beyond security cooperation, Odumegwu-Ojukwu underscored the importance of strengthening partnerships between Nigerian startups and Israeli technology firms to drive innovation and economic growth. She added that Nigeria was interested in leveraging Israeli technology to improve water management and boost agricultural productivity. In his remarks, Freeman reiterated Israel’s commitment to expanding cooperation with Nigeria in innovation, agriculture, healthcare, security, education and skills development. “We are more than willing to work with Nigeria. We know that after the elections, things will be a lot easier. We are committed to defence and security cooperation with Nigeria,” the ambassador said. Freeman described Nigeria as “an amazing country” with warm and welcoming people, adding that stronger engagement between both countries was necessary to unlock the full potential of the relationship. The envoy further noted that annual trade between Nigeria and Israel, estimated at about $200 million, remained below its potential and expressed optimism that both nations would work towards significantly increasing bilateral trade in the years ahead. The post FG seeks Israeli expertise to strengthen border security, combat cross-border crimes appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ActionAid backs Tinubu’s call for people-centred projects over unnecessary flyovers
items.description: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA — ActionAid Nigeria (AAN) has endorsed President Bola Tinubu’s call on state governors to prioritise people-centred projects over the construction of flyovers in areas where they are not needed. In a statement signed by its Country Director, Dr. Andrew Mamedu, the organisation said governments at all levels should focus public spending on projects that directly improve the welfare of citizens, particularly amid prevailing economic challenges. Mamedu described the President’s remarks as an opportunity to broaden the national conversation on public finance and the allocation of scarce resources. “ActionAid Nigeria welcomes President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s recent call on state governors to stop constructing unnecessary flyovers in locations without traffic congestion and instead prioritise projects that directly improve citizens’ lives. “The organisation believes the President’s remarks present an opportunity for a broader national conversation about public finance, one that goes beyond flyovers to address how governments at all levels allocate scarce public resources,” he said. According to him, while infrastructure remains important for development, governments should ensure that public spending reflects the needs of citizens. “At a time when millions of Nigerians are making extraordinary sacrifices amid economic hardship, every naira of public money should deliver measurable value to citizens,” he said. The organisation called on governments to review expenditures on what it described as non-essential projects and reduce spending on luxury acquisitions, oversized official delegations, excessive official travel and other discretionary expenses that do not directly benefit the public. ActionAid also referenced figures contained in the 2026 budget proposal, noting that allocations for official travel, food and refreshments for the President and Vice President could be reviewed to free up additional resources for critical public services. According to the organisation, savings from such expenditure could be redirected to sectors such as education, healthcare and water supply. Mamedu stressed that public budgets should reflect national priorities and improve citizens’ quality of life. He urged governments at all levels to prioritise investments in quality education, primary healthcare, water and sanitation, food security, climate resilience and social protection. The organisation also called for greater transparency and accountability in public spending, including discretionary and security-related expenditure, while respecting legitimate national security considerations. It further urged governments to ensure that infrastructure projects are selected based on evidence, community needs and measurable development outcomes, and to strengthen citizen participation in budget planning, implementation and monitoring. “ActionAid Nigeria urges leaders at every level to seize this moment to shift public spending from prestige to purpose. The true measure of governance is not the number of monuments built, but the number of lives improved through quality education, accessible healthcare, safe water, decent livelihoods and opportunities that enable every Nigerian to thrive,” Mamedu said. The post ActionAid backs Tinubu’s call for people-centred projects over unnecessary flyovers appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: SOUM/DJIBO : la montée des couleurs délocalisée au BIR 22 pour renforcer le lien entre les Forces combattantes et les populations
items.description: SOUM/DJIBO : la montée des couleurs délocalisée au BIR 22 pour renforcer le lien entre les Forces combattantes et les populations Djibo, 3 août 2026 (AIB)-La cérémonie mensuelle de montée des couleurs nationales s'est tenue, ce lundi 3 août 2026, dans l'enceinte du 22ᵉ Bataillon d'intervention rapide (BIR 22) de Djibo, à l'initiative du Haut-Commissaire de la province du Soum, Camarade Wend Néré Wilfried Tougma, en collaboration avec le Camarade Commandant du BIR 22. Cette délocalisation, une première dans la province, vise à renforcer le rapprochement entre les Forces engagées sur le terrain et les populations, dans un contexte de reconquête du territoire national. Habituellement organisée au Haut-Commissariat, la cérémonie s'est déroulée cette fois au sein du BIR 22, également appelé « Bataillon de choc ». Elle a réuni les autorités administratives, coutumières et religieuses, les Forces de Défense et de Sécurité (FDS), les Volontaires pour la Défense de la Patrie (VDP), les partenaires techniques et humanitaires, les organisations de la société civile, ainsi qu'une forte mobilisation des populations. Dans son allocution, le camarade Haut-Commissaire a exprimé sa gratitude au commandement du BIR 22 pour avoir accepté d'abriter cette cérémonie républicaine. Il a salué cette initiative, qu'il a qualifiée de symbole fort du rapprochement entre les Forces combattantes et les populations, dans un contexte marqué par la reconquête du territoire national et le renforcement de la cohésion sociale. Profitant de cette tribune, il a dressé le bilan des principales activités conduites dans la province au cours du mois de juillet 2026. Il a notamment évoqué la tenue de la deuxième session du Cadre de concertation provincial (CCP), consacrée à la cohésion sociale et au vivre-ensemble, l'organisation d'une grande conférence publique sur cette thématique, l'installation du bureau provincial du Conseil des personnes vivant avec un handicap, la vulgarisation des textes relatifs au Conseil national consultatif de la jeunesse (CNCJ-BF), ainsi que la mise en place de son bureau provincial. Il est également revenu sur le lancement des concours directs et professionnels de la Fonction publique, les échanges sur la liberté d'association, le déroulement de la manifestation communautaire « DÉORAL », le lancement des épreuves du Certificat supérieur d'aptitude pédagogique (CSAPe), ainsi que celui de l'immersion patriotique obligatoire des nouveaux bacheliers de la session 2026. Parmi les actions de solidarité et de soutien aux initiatives de développement et de sécurisation figurent le don de trois tonnes de riz et de 30 cartons de savon offert par le 28ᵉ Bataillon d'intervention rapide (BIR 28) aux populations et aux personnes déplacées internes d'Arbinda, l'appui matériel et financier de la commune de Djibo à l'organisation de l'immersion patriotique, le don de 260 litres de carburant remis par la veille citoyenne d'Arbinda aux Volontaires pour la Défense de la Patrie, ainsi que les activités de sensibilisation sur le port du casque et la distribution de casques au profit des agents communaux et des membres de la délégation spéciale de Kelbo. La cérémonie s'est achevée dans une ambiance empreinte de ferveur patriotique et de convivialité. Au-delà de son caractère républicain et symbolique, cette édition délocalisée de la montée des couleurs a illustré la volonté des autorités provinciales de consolider les liens entre les Forces combattantes et les populations, tout en réaffirmant l'engagement collectif des acteurs de la province en faveur du patriotisme, de la cohésion sociale et de la construction d'un Burkina Faso souverain, résilient et prospère. Agence d'information du Burkina AG/ata

items.title: 37 Nigerians repatriated from Türkiye arrive Abuja
items.description: The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) has received 37 Nigerian nationals who returned from the Republic of Türkiye through the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja. In a statement issued on Monday, the agency said the returnees arrived aboard a chartered aircraft following an official notification from the Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs as part of ongoing efforts to facilitate the safe and orderly return of Nigerians abroad. According to NEMA, its Abuja Operations Office activated a coordinated reception process involving government agencies and humanitarian partners to ensure the returnees were received in a dignified and humane manner. The agency explained that the exercise included documentation, profiling, medical screening and the provision of immediate humanitarian assistance before the returnees were referred to the appropriate authorities for reintegration. Speaking during the reception, the Head of NEMA’s Abuja Operations Office, Pharm. Zakari Abubakar, reaffirmed the agency’s commitment to protecting the welfare of returning Nigerians. “At NEMA, our priority is to ensure that every returning Nigerian is treated with dignity, compassion and respect. We encourage our compatriots to embrace this opportunity for a fresh start, remain law-abiding, and take advantage of available government support programmes aimed at facilitating their successful reintegration into society,” he said. Abubakar also praised the collaboration among the various agencies involved in the exercise, noting that inter-agency cooperation remains essential for effective reception and reintegration of returning migrants. NEMA said the operation involved the Nigerian Immigration Service, the National Commission for Refugees, Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons, the Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs, airport authorities, security agencies and other relevant stakeholders. The latest repatriation is part of the Federal Government’s ongoing efforts to assist distressed Nigerians abroad. In June, NEMA received 123 Nigerians who voluntarily returned from Algeria under the Assisted Voluntary Return programme facilitated by the International Organisation for Migration. Earlier in April, the agency also received 181 Nigerian returnees from Tripoli, Libya, under the same initiative aimed at ensuring their safe return and reintegration into society. items.title: Clôture avec succès de JamSalam 2026 du Club Afrique Développement
items.description: La résidence artistique panafricaine JamSalam* 2026 organisée par le Club Afrique Développement d’Attijariwafa bank s’est clôturée le 29 juillet dernier à Al Maqam, Tahannaoute (Maroc), après deux semaines durant lesquelles 15 artistes de 15 pays africains ont créé, dialogué et développé des liens forts de fraternité. Ils en ressortent unis par une expérience d’aucuns qualifient de transformatrice et inoubliable. La cérémonie de clôture et de restitution des œuvres à réuni, aux côtés des artistes, les représentants JamSalam des 15 pays de présence du groupe Attijariwafa bank en Afrique, du Club Afrique Développement et de la Fondation Attijariwafa bank, dans un esprit vibrant de famille. À cette occasion, les artistes, âgés de 20 à 35 ans, ont reçu leurs attestations de participation, après avoir témoigné de l’impact durable d’une telle initiative sur leurs perspectives. Prenant la parole à cette occasion, l’artiste peintre et sculpteur, fondateur de la résidence Al Maqam, Mohamed Mourabiti, tout en saluant l’initiative, a souligné l’enjeu de la création artistique commune, ainsi que l’importance du dialogue intracontinental pour un progrès collectif, ancré dans les territoires. Le thème de la Résidence : « Au Nom de Toumaï, Espoir de vie » a fortement nourri la créativité des artistes, réalisant des œuvres abouties (peinture, sculpture, photographie) que les professionnels présents, comme les invités, ont considéré de grande qualité et d’une grande sensibilité. Durant ces deux semaines, les artistes ont également bénéficié de la guidance et de la direction artistique de M. Ousseynou Wade, Président du Grand Jury de JamSalam, expert culturel et artistique de référence sur la scène africaine. Deux visites culturelles à Rabat et Marrakech ont également permis aux artistes de nourrir leurs regards et leurs inspirations. Les œuvres créées durant la Résidence seront présentées au prochain Forum International Afrique Développement organisé par le Club Afrique Développement d’Attijariwafa bank, puis mises aux enchères au profit d’une œuvre de bienfaisance. La promotion JamSalam 2026 rejoint par ailleurs la communauté du Club Afrique Développement, ce, dans une perspective de collaboration et d’impact durable, au service du progrès commun. Les artistes de la promotion JamSalam 2026 sont : Falhone Ogun-peinture (Bénin), Ali Drabo-photographie (Burkina Faso), Grâce Dorothe Tong-arts pluridisciplinaires (Cameroun), Shams-peinture et design (Congo-Brazzaville), Ouacabessay Kouame peinture (Côte d'Ivoire), Doaa Fakher-peinture (Egypte), Julie Mvie-photographie (Gabon), Maïmouna Toure-peinture (Mali), Yassine Chraïbi-arts pluridisciplinaires (Maroc), Sidi Mohamed Sow photographie (Mauritanie), Ibrahim Harouna-arts multimédias (Niger), Marema-peinture (Sénégal), Emmanuel Koukta-photographie (Tchad), Afi Elikplim-sculpture (Togo), Sabra Ben Fradj-peinture (Tunisie). *Jam et Salam, signifient « Paix » respectivement en Wolof et en arabe. items.title: Apple launches legal appeal over UK demand for user data
items.description: Apple has filed a new legal challenge against the UK government’s latest attempt to gain access to users’ encrypted data, the US tech giant confirmed to AFP on Monday. The dispute stems from a UK government demand that Apple create a “backdoor” to let authorities snoop on data uploaded by Apple users if required, for example by law enforcement agencies. “As we have said many times before, we have never built a backdoor or master key to any of our products or services and we never will,” Apple said in a statement from September, re-shared with AFP on Monday. An Apple spokesperson confirmed the legal appeal, first reported by the Financial Times, but declined to comment further. The UK government did not immediately respond to a request for comment. US media reported last year that the UK had requested access to encrypted data uploaded by any Apple user around the world. The demand sparked tensions between London and Washington, ultimately prompting the UK to drop its request for global access, then-US intelligence chief Tulsi Gabbard said on X in August 2025. The FT reported in October that London had instead requested Apple for access to its British users’ encrypted data — the focus of Apple’s latest legal challenge. Many tech platforms pride themselves on being able to guarantee privacy through encryption of messages and other content, and providing access to law enforcement has long been seen as off-limits. Apple stopped offering its most advanced encryption feature — known as Advanced Data Protection — for British users in February 2025. ADP ensures that only account holders can view content such as photos and documents stored in the cloud through end-to-end encryption. Police officials worldwide say encryption can shield criminals, terrorists and pornographers from prosecution even when authorities have a legal warrant for an investigation. But civil rights and privacy advocates, along with many cybersecurity professionals, praise data encryption as a way to protect against wrongful snooping by authorities as well as hackers. Le général de division Ebaka Hippolyte est nommé major général de l'état-major des armées, le général de division Nka Valère nommé commandant des écoles et centres d'instruction interarmées. items.title: Burkina/Photographie : la 4ᵉ édition de Photos’OR BF met le cap sur la valorisation du patrimoine touristique de la région de Nando
items.description: Burkina/Photographie : la 4ᵉ édition de Photos'OR BF met le cap sur la valorisation du patrimoine touristique de la région de Nando Ouagadougou, 3 août 2026 (AIB)-La 4ᵉ édition de Photos'OR BF, la randonnée photographique du Burkina Faso, a été annoncée au cours d'un point de presse, ce lundi 3 août 2026 à Ouagadougou. Elle se tiendra dans la région de Nando sous le thème « Patrimoine vivant et résilience : la photographie au service de la valorisation touristique et culturelle en temps de crise ». Cette initiative vise à promouvoir les sites touristiques et culturels du circuit Koudougou-Réo-Sabou. « Cette 4ᵉ édition ambitionne de faire de la randonnée photographique du Burkina Faso une référence nationale et sous-régionale, où l'image devient un levier de valorisation du patrimoine, de promotion touristique, de formation professionnelle et d'innovation culturelle », a déclaré le photographe et promoteur de Photos'OR BF, Yempabou Dieudonné Ouoba. Avec pour pays invité d'honneur le Togo, cette 4ᵉ édition se tient sous le thème « Patrimoine vivant et résilience : la photographie au service de la valorisation touristique et culturelle en temps de crise ». Selon le promoteur, du 7 au 9 août 2026, soit 72 heures, 25 photographes en immersion dans la région de Nando produiront un contenu photographique plus riche, plus authentique et plus diversifié du patrimoine culturel et touristique des villes de Koudougou, de Réo et de Sabou. Yempabou Dieudonné Ouoba a révélé que cette édition sera marquée par une exposition photographique qui se tiendra du 17 au 19 août 2026, afin de permettre aux communautés locales de découvrir les œuvres réalisées sur leur propre territoire. M. Ouoba a également indiqué que « des panels thématiques et des échanges d'expériences sont au programme pour favoriser la création de réseaux professionnels et le développement de projets photographiques régionaux ». « Les meilleures photographies réalisées alimenteront une banque d'images professionnelles destinée à soutenir la communication des institutions, des collectivités territoriales et des acteurs du tourisme », a-t-il précisé. Photos'OR BF est une plateforme de promotion de la photographie burkinabè qui œuvre à la formation, à la valorisation du patrimoine, à la création artistique et à la coopération culturelle. items.title: CBCN right to raise concerns over insecurity, economy — Don
items.description: By Kafayat Kokumo The Executive Director of Development Specs Academy, Prof. Okey Ikechukwu, has defended the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria (CBCN) over its recent engagement with President Bola Tinubu, saying the bishops were justified in raising concerns about insecurity, economic hardship and governance. Speaking on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily, Ikechukwu said the bishops were performing their democratic responsibility by conveying the concerns of Nigerians to the President. “What they did is part of what you call the feedback loop for good governance, where interest groups, individuals, institutions and stakeholders take time to raise issues with those who should do something about it,” he said. While acknowledging that President Tinubu also had the right to respond, Ikechukwu said government should focus on strengthening public confidence and addressing citizens’ concerns. On preparations for the 2027 general elections, the development expert welcomed the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) assurances on electoral reforms but cautioned against excessive optimism, citing the experience of the 2023 general elections. According to him, credible elections will depend not only on technology but also on effective institutions and strict enforcement of electoral laws. “I’m not calling for a level playing field. I’m calling for a field with clear rules of engagement, enforceable penalties for misconduct and institutions of state that have credibility,” he said. Ikechukwu also commented on the President’s reported statement that “all is fair in politics,” arguing that politics should be guided by morality, justice and accountability. On the economy, he said although the administration’s reforms may be well-intentioned, many Nigerians were yet to experience tangible improvements in their living conditions. He urged government officials to communicate with greater sensitivity, noting that rising food prices, insecurity and declining purchasing power remain key concerns for many citizens. The development expert also spoke on the renewed public debate over the President’s academic credentials, suggesting that INEC should clearly indicate whether candidates meet constitutional requirements whenever questions arise over submitted documents. He further attributed weak political accountability to both political leaders and voters, warning that vote-buying continued to undermine democratic governance. “When you give somebody money to buy his vote and he accepts it, he has already said it doesn’t matter who you are or what you do for the next four years,” he said. Ikechukwu urged Nigerians to make informed electoral choices through political education, stressing that sustainable democracy depends on responsible leadership and an electorate willing to hold public office holders accountable. items.title: 95 kg de cocaïne interceptés à l’aéroport de Johannesburg
items.description: La police sud-africaine a annoncé, ce lundi 3 août 2026, la saisie de 95 kilogrammes de cocaïne à l’aéroport international O.R. Tambo de Johannesburg. L’information, relayée par plusieurs sources médiatiques, fait état d’une cargaison en provenance du Brésil, dont la valeur est estimée à 28 millions de rands, soit environ 1,7 million de dollars. Les autorités sud-africaines ont porté un nouveau coup au trafic international de stupéfiants. Dans un communiqué publié le lundi 3 août 2026 et repris par plusieurs médias, le Service de police sud-africain (SAPS) a annoncé la saisie de 95 kilogrammes de cocaïne à l’aéroport international O.R. Tambo de Johannesburg. Selon la police, cette importante cargaison, estimée à près de 28 millions de rands, environ 1,7 million de dollars, est arrivée du Brésil. L’intervention des forces de l’ordre a été rendue possible grâce aux renseignements ayant signalé, dès le vendredi précédent, l’acheminement imminent de drogue vers le territoire sud-africain. L’opération a mobilisé l’unité de police de proximité du SAPS basée à l’aéroport, en étroite collaboration avec les services des douanes ainsi que les équipes opérationnelles de Menzies Aviation. La drogue a été découverte dans la zone de fret peu après l’atterrissage de l’avion. À ce stade, aucune interpellation n’a été annoncée. Toutefois, les investigations se poursuivent afin d’identifier les personnes impliquées dans ce réseau de trafic et de procéder à leur arrestation. Pour les autorités sud-africaines, cette saisie illustre une nouvelle fois l’ampleur du défi posé par le crime organisé transnational. Elles soulignent que les réseaux de narcotrafiquants continuent d'exploiter les grandes plateformes aéroportuaires et les circuits du transport de marchandises pour acheminer des stupéfiants, d'où le renforcement des opérations de renseignement et des contrôles aux frontières. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article 95 kg de cocaïne interceptés à l’aéroport de Johannesburg est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Adebayo alleges Tinubu controls ‘Book of Life’ for NASS return tickets
items.description: —- Says 2027 must be free of institutional interference — l contested against INEC in 2023, describes results as charade —Nigeria needs ‘alliance of all Nigerians,’ not just opposition coalition By Dayo Johnson Akure The Social Democratic Party, SDP, presidential candidate in the 2023 election, Adewole Adebayo, has alleged that many National Assembly members failed to secure return tickets because their names were not in “the book of life” allegedly kept by President Bola Tinubu. Adebayo made the claim during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, monitored in Akure, Ondo State. According to him, several lawmakers have been “stripped of their democratic rights.” “He has a book of life. If your name is on it, you’ll win your primaries. If your name is not on that book of life, it doesn’t matter how popular you are with your people. Even if you won the primary, they will remove your name and put someone whose name is in the book of life there,” Adebayo alleged. He accused the Tinubu administration of defeating the purpose of government. “President Tinubu has defeated himself because you cannot fail to defeat yourself as a government if the collective summary of your service is that you have defeated the purpose of government. In three years plus, he has defeated the essence of the republic,” he said. 2023 Election: ‘I Contested Against INEC’ Speaking on the 2023 polls, Adebayo said the contest was against the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, rather than political opponents. He described the outcome as “fraudulent and a charade,” and said anyone basing analysis on the 2023 results was “legitimizing fraud.” “The whole thing was a charade. Nobody should use the number and go to the Villa and govern anybody because you can’t govern out of fraud or manipulation. So, we cannot normalize the number,” he asserted. Focus on Governance, Not Personality Adebayo dismissed calls for a coalition of only opposition parties, saying what Nigeria needs is “an alliance of all Nigerians” to rescue the country from what he termed a failed administration. He also said INEC’s role should be limited to collecting and disseminating information submitted by political parties, not vetting candidates. “The job of INEC is to ensure that political parties submit names, collate the names, and send the information to the general public. INEC is our servant; it is working for the public,” he said. He urged that discourse ahead of 2027 should focus on developmental challenges rather than personalities. “We need to sound the right issues; otherwise, it will become another enlarged version of Big Brother Africa while you discuss personalities and idiocracies,” he added. items.title: AJK information secretary says 7 law enforcement personnel martyred in recent unrest
items.description: Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Information Secretary Muhammad Rashid Hanif on Monday said that seven law enforcement personnel, including those of police and Rangers, were martyred during recent unrest in the region. The now-proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now. Clashes took place between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Rawalakot and Mirpur last week, which reportedly resulted in several casualties. Amid the tensions, elections are being held across the region in three phases , with those in Mirpur (July 27) and Muzaffarabad divisions (Aug 2) marred by rigging allegations by the PPP. In a televised address on Monday, Hanif recalled a press conference held on July 27 where a police official presented weapons allegedly recovered from JAAC members. Hanif said that seven personnel were martyred from the “same weapons”, while 45 personnel suffered serious injuries and “numerous” others sustained minor injuries. He further said that police and Rangers vehicles were also burned. “This confirms that the blacklisted JAAC is sheltering a large number of armed elements and is attempting to undermine peace and the writ of the state,” the information secretary asserted. Addressing allegations by JAAC regarding incidents in Rawalakot and surrounding areas between July 27 and July 31, he said they were not only false but “part of a misinformation and propaganda campaign”, which in itself was part of a broader effort to “undermine public order and the writ of the state”. He went on to stress that “security institutions of the AJK government have demonstrated the utmost restraint and professionalism while maintaining law and order”. The information secretary rejected allegations of unprovoked firing by security forces and withholding bodies, stating that the government had no bodies presently in its custody. “Propaganda being circulated by this banned organisation on social media is misleading and part of an effort to further aggravate the situation,” he added, alleging that JAAC members were involved in blocking or burning vehicles carrying essential supplies and food. Hanif also provided the casualty figures for law enforcement personnel resulting from JAAC’s “violent actions” in recent years, noting one police official was martyred in 2024 and three personnel in October 2025 . “Two armed operatives from this organisation recently admitted in their confession that they were promised Rs10 million to kill one Rangers personnel, which raises serious concerns about the source of this group’s funding,” the AJK official claimed. AJK govt calls BBC report ‘biased’; Al Jazeera’s coverage termed ‘selective’ Hanif also termed a BBC report on the Rawalakot clashes as “angled, biased and contrary to the facts”, saying that the AJK government “rejected” it. “The facts and figures presented in this report are not only incorrect, but they were published without verification or confirmation from the government, police or the civil administration,” he stated, describing the report as “contrary to the ethics of journalism and professionalism”. Contending that videos and press releases from the AJK administration had provided evidence of JAAC possessing modern weapons, he noted that the BBC “should have at least taken the verified evidence into account and published a report based on facts”. Similarly, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting criticised Al Jazeera’s coverage of the AJK elections, accusing the Qatar-based broadcaster of “selective reporting from handpicked polling stations” in Muzaffarabad. In a post on X on Sunday night, the ministry alleged that the media outlet had “sought to misrepresent the AJK elections and the voting process” through “carefully chosen timings and scripted statements from selected individuals”. “Such yellow journalism only confirms the agenda of external actors with vested interests who are attempting to delegitimise this electoral exercise and undermine the popular will of the people of Muzaffarabad and AJK,” it alleged. The publication had reported that the residents of Muzaffarabad were observing a boycott of the polls following unrest in the region, where the proscribed JAAC has been protesting for several weeks. Over the past two months, the regional administration and the JAAC have been at odds over various issues, most notably the committee’s demand to abolish the 12 seats in the region’s Legislative Assembly, which has resulted in protests across the region. The government has accused militant elements “pu­r­­s­u­ing a foreign age­nda and backed by Indian funding” of fomenting the recent unrest in AJK. On June 5, following the announcement of the JAAC’s June 9 strike, the AJK government declared the committee a proscribed organisation and placed it under the First Schedule of the region’s anti-terrorism act (ATA). The next day, AJK authorities launched a crackdown on the JAAC, arresting scores of its leaders and later placing 147 of its activists on the Fourth Schedule of the ATA. Last Wednesday, AJK police said that 26 personnel were martyred this year during incidents of unrest as they accused the proscribed JAAC of deliberately targeting law enforcement agencies.

items.title: Crise de Sebta : l’UE salue l’action du Maroc et propose un soutien financier accru
items.description: L’Union européenne (UE), a apporté un soutien politique déterminant à l'axe Rabat-Madrid dans la gestion de la pression migratoire autour des présides occupés. La présidente de la Commission européenne, Ursula von der Leyen, a officiellement salué la manière dont les autorités marocaines et espagnoles ont maîtrisé la récente vague de traversées massives vers Sebta. Dans une lettre adressée, ce lundi 3 août, au chef du gouvernement espagnol, Pedro Sánchez, la responsable européenne a qualifié le Maroc de partenaire stratégique majeur de l’Union européenne, indispensable dans la lutte contre la migration clandestine et les réseaux de traite des êtres humains. Pour consolider cette dynamique, Bruxelles préconise un renforcement de l’appui financier et technique fourni au Royaume, ainsi que le développement de systèmes d’alerte précoce pour détecter les mouvements inhabituels à proximité des frontières de Sebta et de Melilla. Bien que le document ne chiffre pas encore cette enveloppe, cette prise de position valide l'approche marocaine et conforte la position officielle de Madrid qui loue la coopération de Rabat, neutralisant ainsi les critiques de certains partis et responsables locaux espagnols. La présidente de la Commission européenne met particulièrement en avant la célérité avec laquelle les opérations de rapatriement des personnes entrées à Sebta ont été menées de concert par le Maroc et l'Espagne. Selon l'exécutif européen, cette efficacité coordonnée a empêché le déplacement des clandestins vers la péninsule ibérique et le reste de l’espace européen. Cette réaction intervient alors que le ministère de l'Intérieur marocain a dévoilé l'ampleur de la pression subie, avec environ 40.000 personnes ayant participé aux tentatives de passage vers Sebta, contre 1.135 vers Melilla, des assauts directement attribués par Rabat à la convergence de la désinformation numérique, de l’activisme des passeurs et des interprétations biaisées de décisions de justice espagnoles. Face à l'urgence, Ursula von der Leyen a rappelé que la protection des frontières extérieures est une responsabilité commune qui ne doit pas peser uniquement sur les États de première ligne. La riposte européenne doit ainsi s'articuler autour d'une approche globale combinant la prévention de la migration irrégulière avec les pays d'origine et de transit, le verrouillage des frontières par une surveillance accrue et des barrières physiques, l'activation de systèmes d'alerte précoce, le démantèlement des réseaux criminels et l'accélération des procédures de retour. La responsable européenne avertit que l'UE n'acceptera pas les entrées illégales et refusera que la question migratoire soit instrumentalisée comme un levier de pression politique ou diplomatique. Cette correspondance fait suite à une lettre d'alerte envoyée par Pedro Sánchez, qui s'était plaint des critiques de certains gouvernements européens accusant l'Espagne de défaillance frontalière et réclamant la suspension des arrangements de Schengen avec Madrid. Dès le début de la crise, la Commission européenne a proposé son aide opérationnelle, précisant que Frontex, Europol et l’Agence de l’UE pour l’asile restaient prêtes à intervenir si Madrid en formulait la demande. En plaçant le Maroc au centre des futurs arrangements post-crise, Bruxelles pose ainsi les bases d'un partenariat plus structuré, dont les modalités techniques et financières feront l'objet de discussions lors de la prochaine réunion extraordinaire des ministres de l'Intérieur et de la Justice de l'Union. The post Crise de Sebta : l’UE salue l’action du Maroc et propose un soutien financier accru appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: 180 days in captivity: Kaduna mother, three daughters escape abductors’ den
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo A woman abducted from Ariko village in Kachia Local Government Area of Kaduna State has regained her freedom after spending about 180 days in captivity alongside her three surviving daughters following an escape from their abductors’ hideout. The woman, whose identity was withheld, was reportedly kidnapped while pregnant along with her daughters, aged four, six and 12. According to a statement issued on Monday by security analyst and former Kaduna governorship aide, Reuben Buhari, the woman and her daughters escaped from the camp on Saturday and embarked on a long trek through the bush despite being weak and exhausted. Buhari said the woman gave birth while in captivity, but the newborn reportedly died about three weeks later. He added that the family’s youngest daughter, four-year-old Christy, was ill during the escape. “Her mother carried her on her back, but when she became tired, the 12-year-old sister took over,” Buhari said. According to him, the family trekked until nightfall on Saturday and spent the night in the bush before continuing their journey the following day. Buhari said the four-year-old later died during the trek. He said the mother and her daughters eventually reached a community in Kachia Local Government Area on Sunday, where residents assisted them and arranged medical attention before their planned transfer to Kaduna for further treatment. The security analyst said the woman and her daughters were among residents abducted from Ariko village and neighbouring communities several months ago. He added that 33 other abductees from Ariko, including 11 people reportedly kidnapped from Awon village, were still being held by their captors. Buhari appealed for continued efforts to secure the release of those still in captivity, expressing concern over reports about their welfare. The post 180 days in captivity: Kaduna mother, three daughters escape abductors’ den appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: TOR’s 100,000 barrels per day capacity could bring fairer fuel pricing regime – Energy analyst
items.description: Energy analyst Benjamin Nsiah says achieving the government’s target of increasing Tema Oil Refinery’s (TOR) capacity to 100,000 barrels per day could transform Ghana’s petroleum pricing system and make fuel prices more transparent. Responding to questions on the impact of TOR producing at that level alongside existing refining capacity from Sentuo Refinery, Mr Nsiah said the major benefit would be the possibility of establishing a more predictable and locally driven pricing framework. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Monday, August 3, he explained that increased domestic refining capacity could reduce some of the additional costs currently associated with importing finished petroleum products. “The difference is that there is likely going to be fair pricing of petroleum products locally because all the costs associated with petroleum pricing will be known and also be a bit transparent,” he said. “Total production will be able to meet total demand, thereby issues of premiums being quoted by BDCs will be dealt with. So there is likely going to be fair pricing,” he added. He noted that Ghana’s current petroleum pricing structure relies heavily on international benchmarks because the country imports a significant portion of its finished petroleum products. However, he argued that if TOR and Sentuo Refinery are able to produce enough fuel for local consumption and export, Ghana would need to develop a new pricing regime based on domestic production benchmarks. “But if TOR and Sentuo are able to do what we consume and even export, it means that we need a pricing regime whereby we set our own benchmark prices,” he said. The energy analyst said such a system could help stabilise prices and potentially make petroleum products more affordable for consumers. “These benchmark prices will also help stabilise and make sure our prices are comparatively cheaper. So the issue of fairness in pricing will also come to play when TOR does this 100,000 barrels per day,” he stated. He added that beyond pricing benefits, expanding TOR’s capacity could have broader economic implications through increased industrial activity, job creation and reduced dependence on imported refined petroleum products.

items.title: Making Families Surrogacy Limited announces 16% reduction in IVF costs for 30 days in recognition of World IVF day
items.description: Making Families Surrogacy Limited, an Ibadan-based surrogacy agency, has announced a 16% reduction in the IVF procedure for their surrogacy programs. The cost adjustment will be in effect from July 30 to August 30, 2026 in recognition of World IVF Day. World IVF Day is observed globally on July 25 to raise awareness about infertility, reproductive health, and access to assisted reproductive technologies. In Nigeria, most fertility treatment including IVF and surrogacy is paid out-of-pocket, with limited health insurance coverage. According to the agency, rising healthcare costs have made it increasingly difficult for many couples to access timely care. “As we celebrated World IVF Day, we recognize that affordability remains one of the biggest barriers for Nigerian families seeking fertility treatment,” said Dr. Peace Mmewurum, Fertility Counselor at Making Families Surrogacy Limited. “This 30-day adjustment is aimed at making IVF more accessible and encouraging open, informed conversations about ethical surrogacy options in Nigeria.” During the period, the agency will also publish a detailed guide breaking down the components of surrogacy costs. The guide is intended to address misinformation and help intended parents make informed decisions. According to health experts, infertility affects an estimated 1 in 4 couples in Nigeria. However, stigma, lack of information, and financial constraints often prevent individuals from seeking professional support. Making Families Surrogacy Limited provides ethical surrogacy coordination, legal guidance, and counseling for intended parents and gestational carriers. The 16% reduction applies to new enrollments in surrogacy programs between July 30 and August 30, 2026. The agency stated that it will monitor feedback and inquiries during the period to assess the impact on access to care. For more information about the cost adjustment or to request the surrogacy cost breakdown guide, visit http://www.makingfamiliessurrogacy.com or contact +2349067856123. About Making Families Surrogacy Limited Making Families Surrogacy Limited is an Ibadan-based agency focused on ethical surrogacy services, patient education, legal support, and counseling for families navigating fertility treatment in Nigeria. The organization is committed to transparency, confidentiality, and professional standards in reproductive healthcare. items.title: Incendies : près de 400 interpellations depuis le début de l’été en France
items.description: Selon le ministere de l'Interieur, ces interpellations s'inscrivent dans des enquetes ouvertes depuis le debut de l'ete sur des affaires liees aux incendies . Parmi elles, 36 personnes ont ete incarcerees, soit apres une condamnation a une peine de prison ferme, soit dans le cadre d'une detention provisoire. Alors que plusieurs incendies ont touche ces dernieres semaines la Gironde, l'Aude ou encore la Seine-et-Marne, les autorites rappellent que les conditions meteorologiques ne sont pas les seules en cause. Le ministre de l'Interieur, Laurent Nuñez, avait indique mi-juillet que pres des deux tiers des incendies recenses etaient d'origine volontaire, contre un tiers d'origine accidentelle. Plusieurs dossiers concernent des mineurs. Dans l'Ain, trois adolescents sont soupconnes d'etre impliques dans l'incendie ayant endommage une partie du château de Divonne-les-Bains. Dans le Var, un jeune de 15 ans a ete interpelle apres deux departs de feu a Cuers. En Gironde, un autre adolescent du meme âge est suspecte d'avoir tente d'incendier des broussailles a Sainte-Eulalie. Dans les Pyrenees-Orientales, la commune d'Amelie-les-Bains-Palalda a instaure un couvre-feu pour les moins de 15 ans entre 23 heures et 6 heures jusqu'au 1er septembre, apres l'incendie d'une salle municipale. Deux enfants de 10 et 13 ans ont ete interpelles dans cette affaire. Si les incendies majeurs en Gironde et dans l'Aude sont desormais maîtrises, 36 departements restent places en risque eleve de feux de foret par Meteo-France. Les autorites appellent a la vigilance, rappelant que des reprises de feu restent possibles malgre la stabilisation de plusieurs foyers.

items.title: Burkina : L’association Faso Lagam Taaba offre des vivres aux appelés de l’immersion patriotique obligatoire
items.description: BURKINA-KADIOGO–IMMERSION -PATRIOTIQUE–DON Burkina : L’association Faso Lagam Taaba offre des vivres aux appelés de l’immersion patriotique obligatoire Ouagadougou, 3 août 2026 (AIB)- L'association Faso Lagam Taaba a remis samedi, des vivres à la Présidente de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de l'arrondissement 9, Mme Jocelyne Traoré/Sanon, en soutien aux appelés de l'édition 2026 de l'Immersion patriotique obligatoire (IPO). Selon le président de l'association Faso Lagam Taaba, Adama Compaoré, ce geste s'inscrit dans les objectifs de la structure visant à promouvoir la cohésion sociale et à accompagner les initiatives de renforcement du patriotisme chez les jeunes. M. Compaoré a également précisé que le don comprend une tonne de riz, cinq bidons d'huile et 60 packs d'eau, pour une valeur globale estimée à 600 000 FCFA, qualifiant cette contribution de « modeste participation » à l'encadrement des appelés « Nous sommes venus soutenir l'initiative du camarade capitaine Ibrahim Traoré afin de permettre à nos petits frères et à nos enfants de s'approprier cette tradition burkinabè qu'est le patriotisme », a-t-il déclaré. M. Compaoré a, par ailleurs, invité les autres associations ainsi que les particuliers à emboîter le pas en apportant leur soutien, en nature ou en espèces, afin d'accompagner les efforts du gouvernement dans la mise en œuvre de l'Immersion patriotique obligatoire. La Présidente de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de l'arrondissement 9, Jocelyne Traoré/Sanon, réceptionnant, le don a exprimé sa satisfaction et salué un acte de solidarité qui contribuera à la prise en charge des appelés. Elle a rappelé que l'Immersion patriotique obligatoire, instituée par le Président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, vise à inculquer aux jeunes les valeurs de patriotisme, de discipline, de respect des institutions et d'engagement envers la Nation. Mme Traoré a indiqué que les vivres seront acheminés vers la cellule régionale de l'IPO du Kadiogo, chargée de leur répartition entre les cinq sites accueillant les appelés de l'arrondissement 9. La PDS a également souligné que ce geste traduit un message de solidarité, d'humanisme et d'engagement patriotique à l'endroit de l'ensemble des Burkinabè. Elle appelé les forces vives de l'arrondissement 9, aux associations, aux opérateurs économiques et aux citoyens à poursuivre la mobilisation autour de cette initiative afin de contribuer à la formation de citoyens responsables et à la construction d'un Burkina Faso fort, résilient et prospère. Agence d’information du Burkina NO/YOS

items.title: NACSA deepens collaboration with MMDAs to strengthen community security and prevent gun violence
items.description: The National Commission on Small Arms and Light Weapons (NACSA) has intensified its engagement with local government authorities as part of efforts to strengthen community-based approaches to preventing armed violence and promoting public safety. The Commission said effective control of small arms begins at the community level, making Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) key partners in promoting peace and supporting responsible firearms management. As part of its engagement strategy, NACSA conducted sensitisation programmes for local authorities in the Sekondi-Takoradi Metropolis in the Western Region and the Asuogyaman District in the Eastern Region. The sessions focused on the security implications of illicit small arms proliferation, Ghana’s firearms regulatory framework and the Commission’s mandate in promoting responsible firearms control. NACSA also highlighted the role of elected representatives and local leaders in educating residents, encouraging lawful firearm ownership and supporting initiatives aimed at preventing violence within their communities. The Commission said strengthening partnerships with local authorities remains critical to developing sustainable solutions to emerging security challenges, noting that lasting peace requires collaboration among communities, local leadership and security institutions. NACSA commended the leadership of the Sekondi-Takoradi Metropolitan Assembly and the Asuogyaman District Assembly for their commitment to working with the Commission to build safer and more resilient communities.

items.title: Back-to-back! ‘On A More Serious Note’ retains Comic TV Programme of the Year title
items.description: Joy Prime’s comedy and entertainment programme, On A More Serious Note, has retained its title as Comic TV Programme of the Year at the 2026 Ghana Comedy Awards, cementing its place as one of Ghana’s leading television comedy shows. The programme beat fellow nominees Half Serious Show on UTV and The Real News to claim the award for the second consecutive year, following its first win at the 2025 edition of the awards. The latest recognition comes less than three years after the programme debuted on Joy Prime in December 2023, marking a steady rise for a show that has carved out a niche by blending topical discussions, satire and live comedy. Hosted by KMJ and Amelley Djosu, popularly known as Saminiwaa, On A More Serious Note has become a regular Friday night fixture for viewers seeking a humorous take on the week’s biggest stories. The programme features comedian Eyiram, blogger Xerda and comedian Rubbin Adarkwa as resident panellists, alongside guest appearances from personalities across entertainment, politics, sports and social life. Each episode explores trending issues through discussion, improvisation and comic reenactments, offering audiences a satirical perspective on events shaping public conversation. The programme also opens with a disclaimer reminding viewers that its content is intended for entertainment. The back-to-back award reflects the show’s growing influence within Ghana’s comedy landscape, where television programmes are increasingly competing alongside stand-up comedy, online skits and digital content for audience attention. The Ghana Comedy Awards, organised annually to honour excellence across the country’s comedy industry, recognise achievements in television, radio, digital content, stand-up comedy and acting. The awards have become one of the sector’s key platforms for celebrating performers and productions that contribute to the growth of comedy in Ghana. For Joy Prime, the latest win reinforces the channel’s growing reputation as a flagship entertainment offering. Since its launch, “On A More Serious Note” has built a loyal following by combining current affairs with humour, creating a format that resonates with audiences while encouraging conversations around issues dominating the national agenda. The consecutive victories also underscore the programme’s consistency in a competitive category, strengthening its position as one of Ghana’s most recognised comedy television productions.

items.title: Small Arms Commission concludes armoury storekeepers and managers training to improve weapons management standards
items.description: The National Commission on Small Arms and Light Weapons (NACSA) has successfully concluded an Armoury Storekeepers and Store Managers Course aimed at improving standards in Physical Security and Stockpile Management (PSSM) within Ghana’s security architecture. The Commission said the training was designed to enhance the capacity of personnel responsible for managing armouries, with a focus on promoting safe storage practices, effective weapons and ammunition management, and compliance with international standards. NACSA expressed appreciation to The HALO Trust for its technical support and partnership in delivering the course, particularly in the areas of Weapons and Ammunition Management (WAM), safety compliance and professional development. The Commission congratulated all participants who completed the training and said it expects the knowledge acquired to contribute to improved practices across armouries nationwide. It added that the initiative forms part of broader efforts to strengthen Ghana’s systems for managing small arms and ammunition while reducing risks associated with poor storage and handling practices. NACSA said it remains committed to promoting adherence to international best practices in armoury management and supporting a safer security environment in the country.

items.title: Religious scholar killed in explosion at supermarket in South Waziristan's Wana
items.description: LOWER SOUTH WAZIRISTAN: A religious scholar was killed in an explosion, suspected to have been caused by a pressure bomb, at a supermarket in Lower South Waziristan’s Wana on Monday, police said. Wana Circle Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Asghar Ali Shah told Dawn that the explosion occurred on the ground floor of a supermarket located in Rustam Bazaar. He said Mufti Jana Mir Masti Khel sustained critical injuries in the explosion and was immediately shifted to Wana district headquarters hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries. The DSP added that he and Wana City Police Station House Officer Usman Wazir, along with a large contingent of police, reached the site of the incident after the explosion, and the area was cordoned off while investigators collected forensic evidence. The DSP said preliminary findings suggested that the pressure bomb had been planted in advance with the apparent intention of targeting the cleric. He said police had filed an initial complaint and further investigation was under way to identify the perpetrators and determine the motive behind the attack. In addition to his religious services, Mufti Jana Mir played a significant role in various national peace jirgas held after the 2004 military operations in Wana’s different areas. Most recently, he participated in the Waziristan Peace Jirga, where he presented key recommendations aimed at restoring law and order and achieving sustainable peace in the area. He was widely regarded as a respected religious and social figure who consistently advocated for regional and national interests and worked to promote lasting peace in the region. Monday’s incident comes just three days after unidentified gunmen shot dead Maulana Ismail, a cleric affiliated with Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F), in Azam Warsak Bazaar of Lower South Waziristan’s Birmal tehsil. On July 28, a local cleric was killed and two other people were injured in a suspected quadcopter attack near a mosque in the Landi Doag area of Birmal. In January, JUI-F leader Maulana Sultan Muhammad Wazir was critically injured in a bomb blast near a madressah in South Waziristan’s Wana Bazaar area and later succumbed to his injuries.

items.title: Accords et conventions financiers du Sénégal : Un portefeuille de bailleurs assez diversifié en 2026
items.description: Le Sénégal a pu présenter un portefeuille de partenaires diversifié en 2026, malgré l’absence d’accords avec le Fonds monétaire international (Fmi). Des accords et conventions ont été signés avec notamment la Banque ouest-africaine de développement (Boad), l’Association internationale de développement (Ida), Standard chartered bank, etc. Depuis mai 2024, le Sénégal attend un nouveau partenariat avec le Fonds monétaire international (Fmi). Malgré ce contexte marqué par la baisse de la notation souveraine, l’État a pu compter sur un portefeuille de partenaires diversifié. Selon un document du ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et du Plan, le gouvernement a pu signer plusieurs conventions de prêts et d’accords avec des institutions nationales et internationales depuis le début de l’année 2026. L’une d’elles est la Banque ouest-africaine de développement (Boad). Elle a signé avec le Sénégal un accord de prêt sur 10 ans avec une période de grâce de deux ans. L’opération, d’un montant de 50 milliards de FCfa, est destinée au projet de construction et d’exploitation du segment nord du réseau de transport du gaz naturel par gazoduc. À côté de la Boad, le Sénégal a eu le concours de l’Association internationale de développement du Groupe de la Banque mondiale. La convention a été signée le 5 mai 2026, sur une période 25 ans. L’enveloppe de 22 milliards de FCfa est orientée vers le projet d’amélioration du cadastre et du régime foncier du Sénégal. En 2026, il a également eu comme partenaire financier international Invest international Capital dans le cadre de la construction de l’émissaire en mer de la baie de Hann, à travers une convention de prêt d’un montant de 7,5 milliards de FCfa. Le 21 juillet 2026, l’État a pu nouer un partenariat avec la Société internationale islamique de financement du Commerce (Itfc), branche de la Banque islamique de développement (Bid). L’enveloppe de 26 milliards de FCfa a pour objectif de couvrir des besoins financiers pour la campagne arachidière 2025-2026 et 2026-2027, en faveur de la Sonacos. Le Sénégal a également pu compter sur le partenariat avec Standard chartered bank. En avril, un accord de prêt a été signé avec ce bailleur pour un montant de 151 milliards de FCfa destiné au renouvellement des chaînes de valeur agricoles et à la sécurisation des produits alimentaires. Au total, les accords de prêts et de convention signés avec des partenaires étrangers, entre janvier et juillet 2026, ont représenté plus de 311 milliards de FCfa. Même si l’accord avec le Fmi est attendu, en 2025, le Sénégal a pu signer des accords de financement avec la Banque africaine de développement (Bad) pour 48 milliards de FCfa, la Badea (131 milliards de FCfa), l’Agence française de développement (Afd — près de 50 milliards de FCfa) pour 3 projets. Sans oublier le Fonds de l’Organisation des pays exportateurs de pétrole (Opep) pour un montant de 65 milliards de FCfa. Ces engagements des bailleurs internationaux au sujet de la dette extérieure, suivant le tableau présenté par le ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et du Plan, ont atteint plus de 797 milliards de FCfa en 2025, pour des maturités allant parfois à 30 ans. À côté de ces accords, le Sénégal entend finaliser l’accord avec le Fmi dans l’objectif d’attirer davantage de partenaires et d’investisseurs. Pour 2026, le Sénégal présente des besoins de financement de l’ordre de 6.075 milliards de FCfa. Demba DIENG

items.title: Le Niger sur Kalangou du 03 août 2026
items.description: Listen to « Protection des enfants et certificats de nationalite (Le Niger sur Kalangou) » on Spreaker. Au menu de l'emission : a Gaya, Abdou Maman Kabir, travailleur social a la Direction departementale de la protection de l'enfant et de la promotion de la femme, explique les causes du phenomene et les risques auxquels sont exposes les enfants mineurs voyageant seuls ou confies a des personnes sans garanties suffisantes de securite. La rubrique justice est consacree a l'etablissement du certificat de nationalite, commence le 27 juillet 2026 au tribunal d'instance de Nguigmi. a Niamey, l'echo des regions s'interesse aux activites des eleves pendant les vacances scolaires. Certains se divertissent, tandis que d'autres apprennent un metier ou menent de petites activites commerciales pour gagner de l'argent de poche. La chronique « Lotti » presente les precautions a prendre pour proteger les enfants contre les infections respiratoires, le paludisme et les maladies liees aux eaux stagnantes pendant la saison des pluies.
